page: Microsoft Azure E128ads_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance from the Eadsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core. Additionally, it includes 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data places this server in the top tier (top 10%) across multiple performance dimensions. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 232766.23 and a PassMark CPU score of 131808.85. Memory performance is exceptionally strong, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 11983.28 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 202.2 GB/sec. Database and caching capabilities are highlighted by a PassMark database operations score of 40176.82 and Redis SET operations performing at 171.99 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E128ads_v7 offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput tasks. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training, though it remains highly capable for small-to-medium LLM inference, processing 7B model prompts at 311.0 tokens per second. This profile makes it highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and intensive multi-threaded data decompression.

Lacking a dedicated GPU, it is not designed for heavy graphics workloads but excels at memory-intensive applications. The E128ads_v7 is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, high-throughput web serving, and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks.
